marketing.heroBlurb: {brand} watches your endpoints, certificates and DNS every 30 seconds — then tells the right person the moment something breaks. Own your data, run it anywhere, and give customers a status page they actually trust.
marketing.featuresTitle: Replace the five tools you're duct-taping together
marketing.featuresBlurb: {brand} is one control plane for uptime, latency, certificates and alerting — self-hosted, so the data never leaves your infrastructure.
marketing.feature1Body: HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, ICMP, DNS and SSL-expiry checks — one control plane instead of five tools.
marketing.feature2Body: Slack, email, webhooks and Telegram, with de-duplication — so one outage isn't fifty pings.
marketing.feature3Body: Every query is scoped to an org. Teams share an instance without sharing data.
marketing.feature4Body: p50/p95 response times per endpoint, not just a binary up/down flag.
marketing.feature5Body: Every alert arrives with a plain-English explanation of what likely broke, and where to look first.
marketing.howBlurb: No agents, no sidecars, no YAML archaeology.
marketing.step1Body: Create a project per app or team. Every monitor lives in one, so dashboards and status pages stay organised as you grow.
marketing.step2Body: Point {brand} at a URL, host or cluster. It starts probing on your interval within seconds — no agent to install.
marketing.step3Body: Flip one switch to share a public page grouped by project. Customers see what's up; they never see your internals.
marketing.statusTitle: A page your customers can trust
marketing.statusBlurb: Group domains by project, publish on your own domain, and keep targets, IPs and internals private — only names and status are ever exposed.
marketing.statusPrivacyNote: Targets, IPs and check config are never exposed publicly.
marketing.ctaTitle: Stop finding out from your customers.
marketing.ctaBlurb: Spin up {brand}, add your first domain, and get alerted before anyone opens a ticket.
marketing.ctaFinePrint: Free to start — no credit card.

maintenance.step3Body: Nothing to switch on or off. It starts and ends on its own; when it ends, alerts resume.

apiKeys.revokeConfirmBody: Anything using this key stops working immediately. This cannot be undone — you would need to create a new key and update whatever uses it.

quickstart.metaDesc: Sign up and get your first domain monitored in about five minutes.
quickstart.lead: From nothing to a monitored domain with alerts, in about five minutes.

authentication.metaDesc: Create an API key and make your first authenticated request.
authentication.lead: Every API request carries a bearer token. For anything automated, that token is an API key.

api.metaDesc: Every {brand} endpoint, with fields and examples.
api.lead: Base URL https://{apiHost}. Everything is under /api/v1, takes and returns JSON, and needs an API key.

monitors.metaDesc: Every kind of check {brand} can run, and when to reach for each.
monitors.lead: Seven kinds of check. The type decides what a target means and what counts as a failure.

alerts.metaDesc: Where alerts go, how quickly they fire, and how to stay quiet during planned work.
alerts.lead: An alert nobody sees is a dashboard. An alert that fires constantly is noise people learn to ignore — which is worse, because it teaches them to ignore the real one.

automation.metaDesc: Keep your monitors in your repository and apply them from a workflow.
automation.lead: Keep the domains you monitor next to the code that serves them, and keep the two in step automatically.

plans.metaDesc: What each plan includes, and how pay-as-you-go credit works.
plans.lead: Pay monthly, or by the hour. Both work; neither locks you in.

statusPages.metaDesc: A public page your customers can check instead of emailing you.
statusPages.lead: A page anyone can load to see whether your service is working — so during an incident your inbox is not the status page.

consolePage.metaDesc: Call the live {brand} API from your browser — paste a key and send a request.
consolePage.lead: Call the real API from here. Paste a key, pick an endpoint, send it, read the response — the same request a <link>curl</link> would make, with nothing to install.
